learning_outcomes.text: Introduction to mathematical models and solution methods that can be used to examine vibrations of mechanical systems.
Gaining practical experience in the use of this information.

syllabus_topics: Understanding vibration problems encountered in practice
Basic information about methods used in vibration analysis, their application areas, and limitations
Ability to transition from a real system to a physical model and create a mathematical model from the physical model
Solving the mathematical model and evaluating its results
Defining and solving vibration problems encountered in machines
bibliography: Theory of Vibrations with Applications, W.T.Thomson, 1988.
R.F.Steidel, An Introduction to Mechanical Vibrations, 1989.
Tse, Morse, Hinkle, Mechanical Vibrations Theory and Applications, 1986.
L.Meirovitch, Elements of Vibration Analysis, McGraw-Hill.1986.
